spec.description: Every Sentinel-2 pass over Cuenca, Ecuador, in the last four months from the Earth Search STAC catalogue, with its cloud cover; the map's time bar walks the passes and draws the newest image in its window through TiTiler.

options.content:
# Multitemporal: what was there, and when

The satellite passes over Cuenca every five days, come rain or shine. The time bar under the map is that calendar — **one bar per pass** — and dragging it shows you **the last image that falls inside the window**.

All of it comes from **a single query**: one row per pass, with its date and the link to its COG. The calendar and the imagery are the same table, so dragging asks the server nothing — the choice is made here, and something only changes when you cross a date that has an image. If the window falls between two passes there is nothing to show, and the raster is withdrawn.

Check the cloud cover in the table on the right before drawing conclusions: over the equatorial Andes **most passes come covered**, and that is exactly what makes walking the calendar useful rather than settling for the most recent one.

**The bars above the map are the same calendar, one per pass, as tall as its cloud.** Click one and the map draws that pass; click it again and it goes back to the newest. The shaded band is the map's time window, and it moves when you drag the time bar under the map.

**Cloud cover ≤** drops the covered passes from the catalogue, and because the calendar and the imagery are that one query, the bars leave the time bar at the same moment the rows leave the table. It starts at *All*, so nothing is hidden until you ask for it — and here it is worth being sparing with: when this board was written, the four months it opens on held **30 passes and only two under 60 %**, the clearest of them at 39 %. Below 40 % the calendar empties. Over the equatorial Andes the cut that separates anything is 60 % or 80 %, not 10 %.

spec.rawSql:
-- Una fila por pasada del satélite, cada una con su enlace a la imagen.
-- Esto es a la vez el timeline (kepler monta su filtro temporal sobre `time`)
-- y el catálogo del que sale la escena que se pinta: el panel dibuja la última
-- que cae dentro de la ventana, sin volver a preguntar al servidor.
WITH resp AS (
  SELECT http_get(
    'https://earth-search.aws.element84.com/v1/search'
    || '?collections=sentinel-2-l2a'
    || '&bbox=-79.10,-3.05,-78.90,-2.85'
    || '&datetime=' || $__timeFrom() || '/' || $__timeTo()
    || '&limit=400'
  ) AS r
),
features AS (
  SELECT unnest(json_extract(r->>'body', '$.features[*]')) AS f FROM resp
)
SELECT
  (f->'properties'->>'datetime')::TIMESTAMPTZ  AS time,
  f->>'id'                                     AS scene_id,
  (f->'properties'->>'eo:cloud_cover')::DOUBLE AS cloud_cover,
  f->'assets'->'visual'->>'href'               AS raster_url
FROM features
-- El desplegable recorta el catálogo aquí, así que las pasadas que superan el
-- umbral desaparecen a la vez del mapa y del timeline: son la misma consulta.
-- $cloud llega ya entrecomillado del datasource ('20'); el CAST lo vuelve número.
WHERE (f->'properties'->>'eo:cloud_cover')::DOUBLE <= CAST($cloud AS DOUBLE)
ORDER BY time

spec.description: One query, two jobs: it feeds the timeline and supplies the catalogue of scenes. The timeline's window chooses which one is drawn, in the browser.
spec.title: Sentinel-2 over Cuenca · drag the time bar

spec.description: The most cloud a pass may carry and still enter the catalogue. It is the catalogue's own `eo:cloud_cover`, measured over the whole Sentinel-2 granule rather than over Cuenca, so it is a coarse cut. It starts at *All*, because how covered the passes come is part of what this board is showing.
